reviews.review: Ande, corra e atire sem se preocupar, altamente linear.

PURGE IT IN FLAME! Boom, boom, boom, boom, boom... You'll get familiar with the sound of your chainsword and bolter when fighting Chaos or the Green Tide! Excellent multiplayer (I recommend Exterminatus) and very good story in the campaign! Also who doesn't want to ram his chainsword through some elses guts!

This game's tons of fun for a 40k player.  As of 2 yrs after its release id say mostly just for 40k players. Why? Well theres not many on multiplayer anymore. You can find a match but only in certain gameplay modes, hardly ever in the DLC. The combat is really fun and although the campaign isnt the best ever, its still pretty fun for the story and gunning down tons of foes. Then again, 40k fans seem to be focused mostly on the slaughter of xenos so thats perfect. As for others, its a good introductory and if you want to feel like a tank on legs, get this game. try the demo at least because the gameplay pretty damn fun. Also btw, these space marines were created back in the 80s so they never copied anyone else, its the other way around

FOR THE EMPEROR!  Xeno scum and vile daemons shall die before your blade and bolter!

Welcome to [b][i]Irreverend Opinions[/i][/b] As we take on [b]Warhammer 40k Space Marine[/b].

[h1]The Blurb[/h1]

An imperial forge-world, where machines of war are made, has been invaded by the Ork scum, and it falls on the shoulders of you, a heroic space marine captain, to slaughter them all and save the day.  But wait!  Chaos!

First person linear story shooter, with a multiplayer extension.

[h1]The Good[/h1]

The campaign is both fun and involving, no matter if you're familiar to the setting or not.  The story carries a couple of predictable twists, but also a couple of unpredictable ones also, [spoiler]with a bitter ending after victory has settled[/spoiler].  A worthwhile multiplayer experience lets you continue the enjoyment after the game has been completed.

The weapons are simple to master for most part, and enemies are both varied and run with a decent AI.  The graphics are very high-standard, from environmental detail to droplets and giblets as you stomp on an orc's head, to smoke coming off the weapon.  Sound quality is quite well-rounded, giving in-game speech without being too overwhelming, and without drowning the player in explosion noises.

A very polished piece of work.

[h1]The Bad[/h1]

Whoa, railway much.  The whole game is a corridor shooter.  You can tell that this is simply because of the storyline, which makes up for the fact, but if you want to have a free-roaming sandbox, or even a bit of elbow room, then you'll be left wanting unfortunately.

[h1]The Ugly[/h1]

The final boss battle is purely QTE.  Really, guys?  Stop doing this.

No, really.  Stop it.

[h1]Suggestions[/h1]

Can't say much here, with the game this finished.  The core complaints I have are the nature of the game, which cannot be altered without breaking it; and the ending, which honestly I doubt the developers will find worth their time to alter.  If I had my way, I would encourage the ending being shifted to be more inclined to a shooter battle - which is what the game actually functions as, last I checked.

[h1]The Summary[/h1]

8/10, worth holding onto after the campaign because the multiplayer is enjoyable.  Fun shooter game, if a little restricted, but the story makes up for it.
